matter_reference_date_basis: matter_reference_date field of candidates/matters/M026.json; exam session OCTOBER 2024. Every provision was checked for the text in force in October 2024.
corpus_gaps: The conveyancing convention of investigating a chain of title for thirty years from a good root is a practice rule, not a statutory rule; no provision in the corpus fixes a look-back period for a purchaser's title search. The gold answer therefore grounds the depth of the search on the ten-year prescriptive period in the Prescription Ordinance s.3 and on the registration priority rule, and does not assert a thirty-year rule.
Roman-Dutch common law principles that underlie title examination (nemo dat quod non habet, the effect of a defective chain on a subsequent purchaser) are outside the statute-only corpus.

No corpus provision creates the practical certificates conveyancers call for by name: the street line and building line certificate, the non-vesting certificate and the certificate of non-acquisition. They are administrative products of the Municipal Councils Ordinance, the Urban Development Authority Law and the Land Acquisition Act; the map cites the substantive provisions those certificates report on rather than a provision naming the certificate.

Stamp duty on a transfer of immovable property in Colombo is a provincial levy; the corpus holds the Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990 but no later provincial statute or Gazette rates schedule, so the map relies only on the admissibility rule in s.60 and not on any rate.

The corpus holds no Inland Revenue, Exchange Control or Board of Investment enactment, so tax clearance and inward-remittance documents that a purchaser's lawyer would also call for cannot be supported from the corpus.

The corpus holds the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Acts No. 28 of 2022 and No. 3 of 2024 but no commencement Order or certification date for either, and none for the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024. The two-year validation period in 3-2024 s.6 expires on 25 October 2024, inside the matter reference month, so the standing of the 1994 power of attorney at completion cannot be settled from the corpus alone.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
provisions.relevant_excerpt: be void as against all parties claiming an adverse interest thereto on valuable consideration by virtue of any subsequent instrument which is duly registered under this Chapter
provisions.why_relevant: Priority between competing instruments turns on due registration, so the purchaser's lawyer must call for the vendor's title deeds together with a certified extract of the land registry folio to see what has in fact been registered against the land and in what order. It is the reason the search covers registered instruments and not only the deeds the vendor chooses to produce.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; the corpus records no amendment event on this section, and it stands in the consolidated 1990 edition. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
provisions.relevant_excerpt: all duplicates and copies and all books and indexes kept under this Ordinance may be searched and examined by any person claiming to be interested therein or by his attorney-at-law or agent duly authorized thereto in writing, and certified copies of or extracts from any such duplicate, copy, or book may be obtained if required
provisions.why_relevant: This is the statutory authority for the central document of any title examination: the certified extract of the land registry folio, obtained by the purchaser's attorney-at-law. It also authorises certified copies of registered duplicates where an original deed in the chain has been lost.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927; no amendment event recorded on this section. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every instrument presented for registration shall be registered in the book allotted to the division in which the land affected by the instrument is situated
provisions.why_relevant: Registration counts only if it is in the correct folio or a folio opened in continuation of it with cross references. The extract called for must therefore be of the folio in which the first registered instrument affecting the land was registered and of every connected folio, otherwise the search misses registrations that still take priority.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927, amended in 1974 (Act No. 14 of 1974). The amended text long predates the matter date and is the text relied on.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Documents Ordinance No. 23 of 1927
provisions.relevant_excerpt: affecting or relating to land instituted on or after the 9th day of November, 1917, shall bind a purchaser, unless and until the lis pendens is duly registered under this Chapter
provisions.why_relevant: A registered lis pendens binds a purchaser for valuable consideration. The search of the folio must therefore extend to registered lis pendens entries, and the purchaser must call for particulars of any pending action disclosed, because the company would take subject to the outcome of that action.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1927, amended in 1947. The text relied on is the consolidated text, which stood unchanged in October 2024.
provisions.verifier_note: Excerpt is verbatim but begins after the opening negative of s.11(1) ("No lis pendens ... shall bind a purchaser, unless and until the lis pendens is duly registered"), so standing alone it states the opposite of the section; the section as a whole does support why_relevant, and the corpus OCR renders "lis" as "Us" in subsections (1) and (7).

provisions.formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
provisions.relevant_excerpt: shall be in force or avail in law unless - (a) the relevant deed or instrument shall be in writing, signed by every executant or by any person duly authorised by such executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licenced notary public present at the same time and in the presence of one another, and the same shall be attested by such notary
provisions.why_relevant: No sale or transfer of immovable property avails in law unless it is in writing and notarially attested. Every link in the chain the vendor produces must therefore be a notarially executed deed (or its registered duplicate or a certified copy), which is why the lawyer calls for the deeds themselves and inspects the attestations rather than accepting a schedule of title.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1840; the section was replaced by Act No. 30 of 2022 and further amended by Act No. 4 of 2024, so the text quoted is the text in force in October 2024. The notarial requirement itself has stood since 1840, so the older deeds in the chain were subject to an equivalent requirement in the text then in force. A verifier should confirm the commencement date of Act No. 4 of 2024 against the matter date.

provisions.formal_title: Prevention of Frauds Ordinance No. 7 of 1840
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Provided further, where the transferee is a corporate body and where the Board of Directors of such corporate body is unable to be present and execute the deed or instrument, such Board shall authorise in writing, any other person to sign such deed or instrument on his behalf
provisions.why_relevant: The purchaser here is a corporate body. The transferee must sign and place a thumb impression, and where the board cannot attend, a written board authority in favour of a named signatory is required. That written authorisation, together with proof of the board's constitution, is a document that must be in hand before the transfer is executed.
provisions.temporal_note: This proviso is part of the section as it stood in October 2024, following the 2022 and 2024 amendments. It has no bearing on the older deeds in the chain, which were executed before it was introduced.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and is the text the corpus now prints, but subsection (2) with the corporate-transferee proviso was inserted only by the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024, which carries no commencement provision beyond its short title; the corpus records no certification date, so applicability at the October 2024 matter date cannot be established from the corpus and rests on the inference that an Act numbered 4 of 2024 was certified early in that year.

provisions.formal_title: Prescription Ordinance No. 22 of 1871
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Proof of the undisturbed and uninterrupted possession by a defendant in any action, or by those under whom he claims, of lands or immovable property, by a title adverse to or independent of that of the claimant or plaintiff in such action
provisions.why_relevant: Ten years of undisturbed adverse possession can defeat a paper title, so a deed chain alone does not settle title. The purchaser must also call for documents that evidence possession over at least that period: rates and assessment receipts, utility bills, tenancy or lease agreements and receipts for rent, and where the building is let, the tenancy records.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1871; the corpus records no amendment event on this section (Act No. 26 of 2014 amended the Ordinance but the corpus records no change to s.3). In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
provisions.relevant_excerpt: the transfer of title of any land situated in Sri Lanka, shall be prohibited if such transfer is- (a) to a foreigner; or (b) to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka under the Companies Act where any foreign shareholding in such company, either direct or indirect, is fifty per cent or above; or (c) to a foreign company, unless exempted as provided in section 3.
provisions.why_relevant: The purchaser is a company incorporated in Sri Lanka. A transfer to it is prohibited outright if direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, and s.2(2)(a) requires that the shareholding stay below that level for twenty consecutive years after the transfer. This makes the purchaser's own corporate documents part of the title examination: the share register, the latest annual return and the shareholder particulars needed to establish direct and indirect foreign holding.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2014; the corpus records no amendment event on s.2 itself (the 2017 and 2018 amending Acts touched other sections, and s.3 was amended in 2018). In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
provisions.relevant_excerpt: The provisions of section 2 shall not apply to- (a) any land the title of which is transferred to a Diplomatic Mission of another State within the meaning of the Diplomatic Privileges Act
provisions.why_relevant: The exemptions qualify the prohibition, so if the purchaser were to rely on one (for instance listing on the Colombo Stock Exchange under paragraph (i)) the documents evidencing that exemption would have to be called for as well. On the facts no exemption is relied on, which is why the shareholding documents remain the operative check.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2014, amended by Act No. 21 of 2018. The amended text is the text in force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Companies Act No. 7 of 2007
provisions.relevant_excerpt: A certificate of incorporation issued under this section in-respect of any company, shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that- (a) all the requirements under this Act relating to the incorporation of a company have been complied with
provisions.why_relevant: Both parties are companies, so their existence and identity must be proved by the document the Act treats as conclusive: the certificate of incorporation. Certified copies of the certificate, the articles and the form recording the current directors and registered office are called for to show that the vendor company exists, that the persons signing for it are its directors, and that the purchaser company itself is validly incorporated.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2007; subsections were substituted by the Companies (Amendment) Act No. 13 of 2019. The 2019 text is the text in force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Companies Act No. 7 of 2007
provisions.relevant_excerpt: A company shall not enter into any major transaction, unless such transaction is- (a) approved by special resolution; (b) contingent on approval by special resolution; (c) consented to in writing by all the shareholders of the company; or (d) a transaction which the company is expressly authorised to enter into by a provision in its articles
provisions.why_relevant: A major transaction includes the acquisition of assets worth more than half the value of the company's assets before the acquisition. If the purchase price crosses that threshold for the purchaser, the transaction requires a special resolution, written consent of all shareholders or express authority in the articles. The certified special resolution or shareholders' consent, and the articles, must therefore be called for on the purchaser's side; the same test is applied to the vendor company's disposal of the building.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2007; the corpus records no amendment event on this section. In force in October 2024.
provisions.verifier_note: Excerpt stops at "a provision in its articles" and omits the closing words of s.185(1)(d), "which was included in it at the time the company was incorporated", so the articles limb is stated more widely in the map and in the gold rule than the section allows.

provisions.formal_title: Companies Act No. 7 of 2007
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Registration of a charge under this Part shall constitute notice to all persons of the particulars of the charge entered on the register of charges under this section, but not of the contents of the instrument which creates or is evidence of the charge
provisions.why_relevant: Because registration of a charge is notice to all persons, the purchaser cannot claim ignorance of a charge registered against a corporate vendor. A search of the Registrar's register of charges, and the certificate of registration and instrument creating any subsisting charge, must be called for in addition to the land registry search, together with a letter of release or vacation of the mortgage on completion.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2007; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Companies Act No. 7 of 2007
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Where a company creates a charge to which this section applies, it shall be the duty of the company within the time specified in subsection (3), to cause a copy of the instrument by which the charge is created or evidenced, to be delivered to the Registrar for registration under this Act.
provisions.why_relevant: A charge on land or on any interest in land created by a company registered in Sri Lanka is registrable, so the register of charges is the right place to look for a mortgage granted by a corporate vendor. It tells the lawyer which company filings to call for.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2007; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Western Province Financial Statute No. 6 of 1990
provisions.relevant_excerpt: No instrument chargeable with stamp duty shall be received or admitted in evidence by any person having by law or consent of parties authority to receive evidence or registered or authenticated or acted upon by any person or by any officer in a public office or corporation or bank or approved credit agency unless such instrument is duly stamped
provisions.why_relevant: The land is in Colombo, in the Western Province. An instrument that is not duly stamped cannot be registered or acted upon, so each deed in the chain must be inspected for the stamp or the endorsement of payment, and the stamp duty receipts and endorsements must be called for with the deeds.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1990; no amendment event recorded on this section in the corpus. A verifier should note that the corpus holds no later Western Province statute, so only the admissibility rule and not the current rate is relied on.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but s.60 carries a proviso under which such an instrument may still be admitted in evidence and, where the duty chargeable is Rs. 5,000 or less, acted upon by the Registrar-General on payment of the proper duty and a penalty; why_relevant and the gold rule state the bar as absolute.

provisions.formal_title: Survey Act No. 17 of 2002
provisions.relevant_excerpt: No plan or map or copy or tracing of a plan or map shall be receivable in evidence in any court in Sri Lanka unless such plan or map has been prepared
provisions.why_relevant: Ten perches has to be identified on the ground and matched to the description in the deeds. Only a plan prepared or certified by the Surveyor-General, an authorised registered surveyor or a registered licensed surveyor is receivable in evidence, so the survey plan and, where the identity of the land is in doubt, a fresh survey by a registered licensed surveyor must be called for.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2002; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Municipal Councils Ordinance No. 29 of 1947
provisions.relevant_excerpt: No building constructed after the date of the commencement of this Ordinance shall be occupied, except by a caretaker, until the Council has given a certificate that such building, as regards construction, drainage, and other respects conforms to the provisions of this Ordinance and to the by-laws made thereunder.
provisions.why_relevant: The subject of the purchase is an office building in a Municipality. It cannot lawfully be occupied without the Council's certificate of conformity, so the approved building plan and the certificate of conformity are documents the purchaser must call for before parting with the price.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1947, amended in 1986. The amended text long predates the matter date.

provisions.formal_title: Municipal Councils Ordinance No. 29 of 1947
provisions.relevant_excerpt: be a first charge on the premises in respect of which the same are incurred or made, and shall be paid to the Council by the owner of such premises and his successors in title
provisions.why_relevant: Council expenses of this kind rank with the rates as a first charge on the premises and are payable by successors in title, so they pass to the purchaser. Rates and assessment receipts to date and a Council statement showing that nothing is outstanding must therefore be called for.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1947; no amendment event recorded on this section. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Urban Development Authority Law No. 41 of 1978
provisions.relevant_excerpt: no Government agency or any other person shall carry out or engage in any development activity in any development area or part thereof, except under the authority, and in accordance with the terms and conditions, of a permit issued in that behalf by the Authority
provisions.why_relevant: If the premises are in a declared development area, the building had to be put up under a permit and in conformity with it. The permit, the approved plan and any clearance about street lines and building limits are called for both to confirm the building is authorised and to see what the company may lawfully do with the premises afterwards.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1978, amended in 1982. The amended text long predates the matter date.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
provisions.relevant_excerpt: shall apply to such Province, Administrative District or Administrative Division as the Minister may from time to time, by Order published in the Gazette, specify as an area to which this Act shall apply
provisions.why_relevant: Title registration applies only to areas declared by Order, so the first thing the lawyer establishes is which system governs the land. If the land is in a declared area the documents called for change; on these facts the land is on the deeds register, which is why the deed chain and folio extract are the operative documents.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Registration of Title Act No. 21 of 1998
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Any person, having a Title of Ownership or other interest in a land parcel registered under this Act, may on payment of the prescribed fee, obtain a Certificate of Title in respect of such Ownership or interest, from the appropriate Registrar of Title.
provisions.why_relevant: Where the land parcel is registered under the title system the Certificate of Title is conclusive evidence of title, and it, rather than the deed chain, is the document to be called for. Recorded as background because on these facts the land is not in a declared area.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1998; no amendment event recorded. In force in October 2024.

provisions.formal_title: Powers of Attorney Ordinance No. 4 of 1902
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Every power of attorney executed in Sri Lanka or any other country shall be registered with the Registrar General.
provisions.why_relevant: One deed in the chain was signed by an attorney and not by the owner. The power of attorney under which he acted, its registration particulars and evidence that it had not been revoked at the date of that deed must be called for, because a deed signed without a subsisting authority breaks the chain.
provisions.temporal_note: The section was repealed and substituted by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022, so the text quoted is the text in force in October 2024. The 1994 deed in the chain was governed by the earlier text, which a verifier should check separately before treating the current registration duty as applicable to that deed.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording is verbatim, but s.3 in this form is the substitution made by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022 and cannot be applied directly to the 1994 deed; the transitional and validation provisions that govern a pre-2022 power at the matter date (28-2022 s.8 and 3-2024 s.6) were missing and have been added as PROV-M026-902 and PROV-M026-903. The corpus body also carries the subsection (1) marker only as "(a)", an OCR loss.

provisions.formal_title: Land Acquisition Act No. 9 of 1950
provisions.relevant_excerpt: Where the Minister considers that a particular land is suitable for a public purpose, or that a particular servitude over a particular land should be acquired for a public purpose, he shall direct the acquiring officer of the district in which that land is situated to cause a notice in accordance with subsection (3) to be given to the owner or owners of that land
provisions.why_relevant: Land in Colombo may be under notice of intended acquisition, and the notice goes to the owner. The purchaser must therefore call on the vendor to produce any notice received and obtain confirmation from the acquiring officer that no acquisition proceeding affects the land, since an acquisition would defeat the purpose of the purchase.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1950, amended in 1964. The amended text long predates the matter date.
provisions.verifier_note: Wording is verbatim and supports the point that a notice of intended acquisition is given to the owner, but s.4 creates no right to obtain confirmation from the acquiring officer that no acquisition proceeding affects the land, which is the document the answer actually calls for; that step is conveyancing practice, not this section.

provisions.formal_title: Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act No. 38 of 2014
provisions.relevant_excerpt: it shall be the duty of the Registrar of Lands to confirm himself whether the foreign shareholding of such company is less than fifty per cent, by requiring the secretary of such company to submit documentary proof
provisions.why_relevant: This is the provision that actually puts the purchaser company's shareholding documents on the list. The Registrar of Lands may not register a transfer caught by s.2 unless satisfied that it complies with the Act, and where the transferee is a Sri Lankan company with foreign shareholding below fifty per cent the Registrar must require the company secretary to produce documentary proof of that shareholding. The map cited only ss.2 and 3, which state the prohibition and the exemptions but require no document.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2014; the corpus records no amendment event on s.4. In force in October 2024.
provisions.verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the link between the foreign shareholding prohibition and the documents called for on the purchaser's side.

provisions.formal_title: Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 28 of 2022
provisions.relevant_excerpt: every power of attorney executed prior to the date of commencement of this Act which has not been registered under the provisions of section 3 of the principal enactment and which has not been revoked or cancelled on or prior to the date of commencement of this Act, shall, within a period of six months from the date of commencement of this Act, be submitted for registration to the Registrar General
provisions.why_relevant: The chain contains a 1994 deed signed under a power of attorney. The registration duty in s.3 of the Ordinance is the 2022 substitution and does not apply of its own force to a power granted in 1994; this transitional provision is what carries an unregistered pre-2022 power into the current regime, and subsection (2) deems it null and void if it was not submitted for registration in time. It is the provision that tells the purchaser's lawyer what to ask about that power and what the answer costs.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2022; the Act carries only a short title, so it operated from the date it became an Act. Its effect on pre-25 October 2022 powers is modified by the Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024 s.6, recorded as PROV-M026-903.
provisions.verifier_note: Added by the verifier: the temporal bridge PROV-M026-021 needed for the 1994 deed.

provisions.formal_title: Powers of Attorney (Amendment) Act No. 3 of 2024
provisions.relevant_excerpt: every power of attorney executed prior to October 25, 2022 and which has not been registered on or prior to the date of commencement of this Act shall be deemed to be valid for a period of two years from October 25, 2022, and be submitted for registration to the Registrar General within such period of two years
provisions.why_relevant: This fixes the deadline that matters on these facts. An unregistered power executed before 25 October 2022 is deemed valid only for two years from that date, that is until 25 October 2024, and is null and void afterwards. Completion is intended for October 2024, so whether the 1994 power was registered, and when, is a question the purchaser's lawyer must put and document before that date rather than a formality.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 2024; the Act carries only a short title, so it operated from the date it became an Act. The two-year period it creates runs from 25 October 2022 and expires in the month of the matter reference date.
provisions.verifier_note: Added by the verifier: decisive temporal provision for the power of attorney limb at an October 2024 completion.

provisions.formal_title: Powers of Attorney Ordinance No. 4 of 1902
provisions.relevant_excerpt: submit such document referred to in paragraph (b) to the Registrar General, to register the same in the relevant volume and folio with cross reference to the volume and folio in which such power of attorney was registered
provisions.why_relevant: The answer calls for evidence that the power of attorney had not been revoked when the 1994 deed was signed, an element no cited provision supported. This is the provision that makes such evidence obtainable: a revocation or cancellation must be executed before a notary and registered in the relevant volume and folio with a cross reference to the folio in which the power was registered, so the registry search is where the absence of a revocation is established.
provisions.temporal_note: The section was substituted by Act No. 28 of 2022 and amended again by Act No. 3 of 2024, so the text quoted is the text in force in October 2024; the revocation regime in 1994 was different and a lawyer should check the position for that deed separately.
provisions.verifier_note: Added by the verifier: supports the 'unrevoked at that date' element of CL-M026-Q01-021.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question asks which documents should be called for on an investigation of title and why. Every document in the answer is called for because a statutory provision makes it necessary: notarial execution and the corporate transferee's written authority under the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2, registration priority, folio registration, lis pendens and the right of search under the Registration of Documents Ordinance ss.7, 11, 14 and 42, possessory evidence because of the Prescription Ordinance s.3, corporate documents and the charge search under the Companies Act ss.5, 102, 105 and 185, the foreign shareholding check under the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.2, stamping under the Western Province Financial Statute s.60, the plan under the Survey Act s.13, and the municipal and development certificates under the Municipal Councils Ordinance ss.127 and 152 and the Urban Development Authority Law s.8J. No judicial authority or common law doctrine is needed to say what to call for or why. The one practice element that is not statutory, the conventional thirty-year look-back, is recorded in corpus_gaps and is deliberately not asserted in the answer; the depth of the search is grounded instead on the ten-year prescriptive period and the registration rule.

legal_issues.issue: Which documents of title and which registry and survey records must be called for to establish that the vendor can convey a clear and marketable title to the land and the office building.
What must be called for to disclose encumbrances: registered instruments and lis pendens on the land registry folio, and charges registered against a corporate vendor with the Registrar of Companies.

What corporate documents are required on both sides so that the transfer is validly executed and is not prohibited, given that the purchaser is a company incorporated in Sri Lanka with foreign shareholders and the price may make the purchase a major transaction.

What planning, building and local authority documents must be called for in respect of an office building within a Municipality and a declared development area, including outstanding charges on the premises.

questions.hop_count_basis: Three necessary linked steps across enactments. Step one: the deeds must be notarially executed to avail in law (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2) and duly registered to hold priority (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.7), which is what makes the deeds, the folio extract and the lis pendens search necessary and fixes the right folio to search (s.14, s.42, s.11). Step two: paper title is not conclusive because of the ten-year prescriptive period (Prescription Ordinance s.3), so possessory documents are required as well. Step three: because both parties are companies, the transfer engages a separate register and separate authorities: incorporation and charge registration under the Companies Act ss.5, 102 and 105, the major transaction rule in s.185, the corporate transferee's written authority under the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(2)(a), and the prohibition on transfer to a company with fifty per cent or more foreign shareholding under the Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.2 read with the exemptions in s.3.

enrichment.original_background: The said Tea Exports (Private) Limited needs to purchase an office building situated in Colombo. Ten Perches (AO, RO, P10) in extent.
enrichment.enriched_background: Tea Exports (Private) Limited, a company incorporated in Sri Lanka, needs to purchase an office building situated in Colombo, ten perches (A0, R0, P10) in extent. The premises are Assessment No. 118, Sir James Peiris Mawatha, Colombo 02, within the administrative limits of the Colombo Municipal Council and within a declared development area; the building was put up in 2013. The land is depicted as Lot 1 in Plan No. 4372 dated 12 August 2011 made by a registered licensed surveyor, and the boundaries have not been checked on the ground since. The seller is Galle Face Holdings (Private) Limited, a company incorporated in Sri Lanka, which is in possession and holds the premises as registered proprietor. Its own title is under Deed of Transfer No. 3128 attested on 4 February 2012 by a notary practising in Colombo; the only earlier instruments produced so far are Deed of Transfer No. 1476 of 1994 and Deed of Gift No. 812 of 1986, and nothing before 1986 has been shown. Deed No. 1476 of 1994 was signed for the then owner by an attorney and not by the owner himself. The premises are mortgaged to a licensed commercial bank under Mortgage Bond No. 2205 of 2019, and the seller filed particulars of that mortgage with the Registrar of Companies. Two of the five shareholders of Tea Exports (Private) Limited are foreign nationals who hold thirty-five per cent of the issued shares between them, and the agreed price of Rs. 480 million is more than half the value of the assets of Tea Exports (Private) Limited before the acquisition. The Council carried out drainage improvement works on the premises in 2022, part of the recoverable cost is still unpaid, and rates receipts have been produced only up to 2021. The land registry for Colombo keeps the land on a deeds folio, and no order has been produced bringing it under the title registration system. Completion is intended for October 2024, and the seller has produced nothing about any intended acquisition of the land by the State.

added_facts.fact: The seller is Galle Face Holdings (Private) Limited, a company incorporated in Sri Lanka, which is in possession and holds the premises as registered proprietor.
added_facts.reason: The original scenario names only the purchaser. Whether the seller is an individual or a company decides whether the company registers and the corporate execution documents come into the title examination at all.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the seller were an individual, the certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and the search of the Registrar's register of charges would fall away and the encumbrance search would rest on the land registry folio alone.

added_facts.fact: The premises are Assessment No. 118, Sir James Peiris Mawatha, Colombo 02, within the administrative limits of the Colombo Municipal Council and within a declared development area, and the building was put up in 2013.
added_facts.reason: The original background says only that the building is in Colombo. Identifying the local authority and the declared development area, and dating the building, is what makes the local authority and planning documents necessary.
added_facts.counterfactual_effect: If the premises were outside a Municipality and outside a declared development area, the certificate of conformity and the development permit would not be called for and the local authority search would be against a different authority.

added_facts.fact: The land is depicted as Lot 1 in Plan No. 4372 dated 12 August 2011 made by a registered licensed surveyor, and the boundaries have not been checked on the ground since.
added_facts.reason: Ten perches has to be tied to a described lot for the extent stated in the deeds to be verifiable. The plan gives the scenario a determinate description without deciding any issue.

gold_answer_draft.issue: What documents should the purchaser's lawyer call for to examine title before Tea Exports (Private) Limited buys the ten perch property with the office building in Colombo, and what is the reason for each. Three groups arise: documents proving the seller's title and the extent of the land, documents disclosing encumbrances and claims, and documents dealing with the corporate capacity of the two companies and with the local authority and planning position of the building.
gold_answer_draft.rule: No sale or transfer of immovable property avails in law unless the deed is in writing, signed by the executants and the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary and attested by him, and where the transferee is a corporate body whose board cannot attend, the board must authorise a signatory in writing (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2(1)(a) and s.2(2)(a)). An unregistered instrument is void against a later instrument taken for valuable consideration and duly registered (Registration of Documents Ordinance s.7), registration counts only if made in the proper folio or a folio opened in continuation of it (s.14), a lis pendens does not bind a purchaser until registered (s.11), and any person interested, or his attorney-at-law, may search the books and obtain certified copies and extracts (s.42). Paper title is not conclusive, because ten years of undisturbed and uninterrupted adverse possession founds a title (Prescription Ordinance s.3). An instrument that is not duly stamped may not be registered or acted upon (Western Province Financial Statute s.60), and a plan is receivable in evidence only if prepared or certified as the Survey Act s.13 requires. Where a company creates a charge on land it must deliver the instrument to the Registrar for registration (Companies Act s.102), and registration is notice of the particulars of the charge to all persons (s.105). A certificate of incorporation is conclusive evidence of incorporation (s.5), and a company may not enter into a major transaction, which includes acquiring assets worth more than half the value of its assets before the acquisition, except by special resolution, unanimous written shareholder consent or express authority in its articles (s.185). Transfer of land to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka is prohibited where direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, unless an exemption in s.3 applies (Land (Restrictions on Alienation) Act s.2). A building in a Municipality may not be occupied until the Council certifies conformity (Municipal Councils Ordinance s.127), council expenses of the kind described are a first charge on the premises payable by successors in title (s.152), development activity in a declared development area requires a permit (Urban Development Authority Law s.8J), and land may be under notice of intended acquisition given to the owner (Land Acquisition Act s.4). Where land lies in an area declared under the Registration of Title Act s.1, the Certificate of Title under s.37 replaces the deed chain, and a registered power of attorney is required for a deed signed by an attorney (Powers of Attorney Ordinance s.3).
gold_answer_draft.application: Since the land is on a deeds folio in Colombo and not in a declared title registration area, the deed chain governs. The seller has produced only three instruments, the latest being Deed of Transfer No. 3128 of 2012 and the earliest Deed of Gift No. 812 of 1986; earlier deeds, or their registered duplicates or certified registry copies, must be called for so that the chain runs back well beyond any period in which a possessory title could have been perfected, and each deed must be inspected for the notarial attestation and for the stamp or endorsement of payment. A certified extract of the land registry folio and of every folio connected to it by cross reference must be called for, because that alone will show the mortgage bond of 2019, any other registered instrument taking priority, and any registered lis pendens. Because Deed No. 1476 of 1994 was signed by an attorney, the power of attorney, its registration particulars and evidence that it was unrevoked at that date must be produced. Plan No. 4372 of 2011 and a certified copy must be called for and, since the boundaries have not been checked on the ground, a fresh survey by a registered licensed surveyor is prudent to confirm that the ten perches match the description in the deeds and that the building stands within the boundaries. Possession must be proved independently of the deeds by rates and assessment receipts, utility bills and the tenancy or lease records for the office building. Because the seller is a company, certified copies of its certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and the resolution authorising the sale must be called for, a search made of the Registrar's register of charges, and the certificate of registration of the 2019 charge, the mortgage bond and the bank's letter agreeing to release the mortgage on payment obtained. On the purchaser's side, the certificate of incorporation, the articles, the share register and the latest annual return must be produced to show that direct and indirect foreign shareholding stands at thirty-five per cent and so below the prohibited level, and since the price of Rs. 480 million exceeds half the value of the company's assets, the special resolution or written consent of all shareholders approving the acquisition, together with the written board authority for the signatory to the transfer, must be in hand before execution. As the building was put up in 2013 within the Municipality and a declared development area, the approved building plan, the development permit and the certificate of conformity must be called for, along with a council statement of rates and other charges, which will disclose the unpaid drainage works expenses and the gap in rates receipts after 2021, and confirmation about street lines and building limits. Confirmation must also be obtained that no notice of intended acquisition affects the land, since none has been produced.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The purchaser's lawyer should call for, and give the following reasons for: the seller's deed and the prior deeds or their registered duplicates and certified registry copies, going back far enough to exclude a possessory claim, because only a notarially executed and duly registered chain gives priority; a certified extract of the land registry folio and connected folios, covering registered instruments and lis pendens, because registration decides priority and a registered pending action binds a purchaser; the power of attorney for the 1994 deed; the survey plan, a certified copy and if necessary a fresh survey, because only a properly certified plan is receivable in evidence and the extent must match the deeds; possessory documents, being rates receipts, utility bills and tenancy records, because ten years of adverse possession can defeat a paper title; stamp endorsements and receipts on every deed, because an unstamped instrument cannot be registered or acted upon; the seller company's certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and authorising resolution, a search of the Registrar's register of charges and the release of the registered mortgage, because registration of a charge is notice to all persons; the purchaser company's certificate of incorporation, articles, share register and annual return, because a transfer to a company with fifty per cent or more foreign shareholding is prohibited, together with the special resolution or unanimous written shareholder consent for what is a major transaction and the written board authority for the signatory; and the approved building plan, development permit, certificate of conformity, council rates and charges statement, street line and building limit confirmation, and confirmation that no acquisition proceeding affects the land. Title should not be accepted until the outstanding council expenses are settled or retained from the price and the mortgage is released on completion.

answer_claims.claim_text: A sale or transfer of immovable property does not avail in law unless the deed is in writing, signed by every executant and the witnesses in the presence of a licensed notary and attested by him, so every link in the chain produced must be a notarially executed deed.

An instrument that is not duly registered is void against a subsequent instrument taken for valuable consideration and duly registered, so the deeds must be checked against what is actually registered on the folio.

A person interested in the land, or his attorney-at-law, may search the registry books and indexes and obtain certified copies and extracts, which is the authority for calling for a certified folio extract and for certified copies of registered duplicates of missing deeds.

Registration is effective only in the folio in which the first registered instrument affecting the land was registered or in a folio opened in continuation of it with cross references, so the extract called for must cover every connected folio.
A registered lis pendens binds a purchaser for valuable consideration, so the search must extend to registered pending actions and particulars of any disclosed action must be called for.
Ten years of undisturbed and uninterrupted possession adverse to the paper owner founds a title, so documents evidencing possession must be called for in addition to the deeds.

An instrument chargeable with stamp duty may not be registered or acted upon unless duly stamped, so each deed must carry the stamp or the endorsement of payment and the receipts must be produced with it.

A plan or map is receivable in evidence only if prepared or certified by the Surveyor-General, an authorised registered surveyor or a registered licensed surveyor, so the plan called for must satisfy that requirement.

A charge on land created by a company must be delivered to the Registrar for registration, and registration is notice to all persons of the particulars of the charge, so a search of the register of charges is required where the seller is a company.

A certificate of incorporation is conclusive evidence that the company was incorporated and that the incorporation requirements were met, which is why it and the articles and current directors' particulars are called for from each company.

A company may not enter into a major transaction, which includes acquiring assets worth more than half the value of its assets before the acquisition, unless it is approved by special resolution, consented to in writing by all shareholders or expressly authorised by its articles.
Transfer of land to a company incorporated in Sri Lanka is prohibited where direct or indirect foreign shareholding is fifty per cent or above, unless one of the statutory exemptions applies.
Where the transferee is a corporate body whose board cannot attend to execute the deed, the board must authorise a signatory in writing, so that written authority must be obtained before execution.

A building in a Municipality may not be occupied until the Council certifies that it conforms to the Ordinance and the by-laws, and development activity in a declared development area requires a permit, so the approved plan, permit and certificate of conformity are called for.

Council expenses of the kind described rank with the rates as a first charge on the premises and are payable by the owner and his successors in title, so a council statement of rates and charges must be called for.
A power of attorney must be registered with the Registrar-General, so where a deed in the chain was signed by an attorney the power and its registration particulars must be produced.
Land may be under a notice of intended acquisition given to the owner, so the purchaser must call for any such notice and for confirmation that no acquisition proceeding affects the land.

Title registration applies only to areas declared by Order, and in a declared area the Certificate of Title is the document to be called for; since this land remains on a deeds folio, the deed chain and folio extract govern.

Because the seller has produced only the 2012, 1994 and 1986 instruments, the earlier deeds or their registered duplicates or certified registry copies must be called for so that the chain runs back beyond any period in which a possessory title could have matured.

A certified extract of the Colombo land registry folio and of every folio connected to it must be called for, since that is what will disclose the 2019 mortgage bond, any competing registered instrument and any registered lis pendens.
Because the 1994 deed was signed by an attorney, the power of attorney, its registration particulars and evidence that it was unrevoked at that date must be produced before that link is accepted.

Plan No. 4372 of 2011 and a certified copy must be called for, and because the boundaries have not been checked on the ground a fresh survey by a registered licensed surveyor should be obtained to confirm that the ten perches and the building match the description in the deeds.

Since the seller is a company that filed particulars of the 2019 mortgage with the Registrar of Companies, its certificate of incorporation, articles, directors' particulars and authorising resolution must be called for, a search made of the register of charges, and the bank's release of the mortgage obtained on completion.

The purchaser's share register and latest annual return must be produced to establish that direct and indirect foreign shareholding stands at thirty-five per cent, below the level at which a transfer to the company would be prohibited.

Because the price of Rs. 480 million exceeds half the value of the purchaser's assets before the acquisition, a certified special resolution or the written consent of all its shareholders, together with the articles and the written board authority for the signatory, must be in hand before the transfer is executed.

As the building was put up in 2013 within the Municipality and a declared development area, the approved building plan, the development permit and the certificate of conformity must be called for, and the council statement will disclose the unpaid drainage works expenses and the gap in rates receipts after 2021.
Since nothing has been produced about any intended State acquisition, confirmation must be obtained from the acquiring officer that no acquisition proceeding affects the land.

The documents to be called for are the chain of notarially executed deeds with their registration and stamp endorsements, a certified folio extract covering registered instruments and lis pendens, the power of attorney for the 1994 deed, the survey plan and if necessary a fresh survey, possessory documents such as rates receipts, utility bills and tenancy records, the corporate documents and charge search for the seller company with the release of the mortgage, the purchaser company's incorporation, shareholding and resolution documents with the written board authority, and the building plan, development permit, certificate of conformity, council rates and charges statement, street line confirmation and confirmation that no acquisition affects the land.

Title should not be accepted, and the price should not be paid over, until the outstanding council expenses are settled or retained and the registered mortgage is released on completion, because both would otherwise bind the company as successor in title.

questions.block_reason: Two grounds, neither of which the verifier can close from the corpus. First, part of the answer is conveyancing practice rather than statute: no corpus provision fixes the depth of the title search, and none creates the acquisition clearance, the street line and building limit confirmation, the bank's letter of release or the fresh survey that the answer calls for, so a complete answer does not follow from statute alone even though each document can be given a statutory reason. The nine claims marked disputed are the ones affected. Second, PROV-M026-006, an indispensable provision, exists only because of the Prevention of Frauds (Amendment) Act No. 4 of 2024, whose commencement date cannot be recovered from the corpus and which falls in the same year as the matter reference date. authority_requirement is left at statute_only because the missing element is practice rather than case law; a lawyer should decide whether it becomes mixed_statute_and_case, in which case the question must be reserved.
